title: Where Will the Ball Fall
description:
You have a 2D box of size `m x n` represented by an integer matrix `grid`, open at both the top and bottom. Each cell contains a diagonal board spanning two opposite corners:
- `1` redirects a ball to the **right** (from top-left to bottom-right).
- `-1` redirects a ball to the **left** (from top-right to bottom-left).

We drop `n` balls simultaneously, one at the top of each column `0, 1, ..., n - 1`. A ball gets stuck and cannot fall further if it hits either side wall of the box or lands in a `'V'`-shaped pocket formed by a `1` immediately to the left of a `-1`.

Return an integer array `answer` of length `n`, where `answer[j]` is the column where the ball dropped from column `j` exits the bottom, or `-1` if it gets stuck.
hints: Simulate each ball independently from row 0 down to row m - 1, tracking its current column col.
At cell (r, col) with direction d = grid[r][col], the ball advances to nextCol = col + d only if 0 <= nextCol < n and grid[r][nextCol] == d; otherwise it gets stuck.

examples.explanation: Only the ball dropped at column 0 navigates through all 5 rows and exits at column 1; all other balls get trapped in V-pockets or walls.
A single column box always pushes the ball into a side wall, returning [-1].
The first five balls exit cleanly at columns 0 through 4, while the ball dropped at column 5 hits the right wall on row 0 and returns -1.
